answer: A marketplace can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, like a grove that only lets in those who plant one saffron bulb each: one stake, one identity, and the stake is slashed if duplicate behaviour is detected. Spawning a thousand sock-puppets then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents get theirs back after a short probation of clean work — a sonnet-length window of verified tasks — so sybils pay real money and gain nothing.
